issues.rule: State machine: a branch omits a side-effect that other branches perform (checklist 23, 19)
issues.problem: The new guard `if (statusTracker.shouldContinue()) position = filePointer` skips the update whenever readSection calls requestTermination(). The only termination path that now sets position itself is LEGACY_END_OF_SEGMENT_MARKER (line 447). Other paths also terminate and leave position stale: the 'Not enough bytes left for another mutation in this CommitLog section' early return (line ~436), which is the normal fewer-than-4-bytes tail case, and the tolerated-error branches that call requestTermination. In these cases the loop breaks, and the post-loop `shouldContinue()` block is also skipped. Position stays at the previous section end (or at 0, or at the start marker). Result.isFullyRead() (log.completed() && marker.position >= maxOffset) stays false for a completed log, and the listener is handed a stale marker. This is the same symptom as the bug being fixed: CdcScannerBuilder never moves past that log. Before the patch, position was always updated to the file pointer after each section.
issues.fix: Handle termination explicitly. Set position to reader.getFilePointer() for benign terminations such as the short tail, or set position to log.maxOffset() when a normal end-of-data termination is reached on a completed log. Keep the position unchanged only for real error terminations. Add a test with a segment whose last section ends fewer than 4 bytes from the end.

also_fixes.fix: In the `< 4` bytes branch, set `this.position = (int) reader.getFilePointer()`, or `log.maxOffset()` when this is the last section, before `requestTermination()`. Alternatively, track clean end-of-section separately from the error flag and update position in both cases.

On that short-tail branch, set `this.position = (int) reader.getFilePointer()` (or the section end) before requestTermination(), or make the guard distinguish benign termination from error termination.

Set this.position = (int) reader.getFilePointer() (or log.maxOffset() when end of the segment is reached) in the 'not enough bytes left' branch before requestTermination(). lenses.summary: Small patch in BufferingCommitLogReader (four-zero bridge) plus a test change. It sets `position` to `startMarker.position()` after the seek, only advances `position` from the file pointer when `statusTracker.shouldContinue()`, sets `position = log.maxOffset()` after the segment loop ends normally, and also sets it when the legacy end-of-segment marker is hit. I read the whole diff and the surrounding reader and `CommitLogReader.Result.isFullyRead` (`log.completed() && marker.position >= log.maxOffset()`). I applied the logic.md and boundary.md checklists from the bundle plus the analytics `### cass-logic-boundary` lens notes (they cover option lookup, CL/DC, token ranges and RF parsing and do not apply to this patch). findings.rule: Conditions/boundaries: guard on shouldContinue() skips the position update on non-end-marker early terminations
findings.problem: The new guard `if (statusTracker.shouldContinue()) position = reader.getFilePointer()` skips the update on every early termination, but only the LEGACY_END_OF_SEGMENT_MARKER branch (line ~447) now sets position itself. The `end - reader.getFilePointer() < 4` branch in readSection (around line 432) calls `requestTermination()` with no position update. This is the case where the last mutation ends less than 4 bytes before the section end. In that case `error` is set, the section loop breaks, and the post-loop `maxOffset` assignment is also skipped. `position` therefore stays at the previous section's end (or 0 or the start marker). The listener is handed a marker at that stale position, and `isFullyRead()` stays false. Before the patch the file pointer was recorded in this case, so this is a regression, although the trigger is rare (the code comment ties it to 2.1-era logs).
findings.fix: In the `< 4` bytes branch, set `this.position = (int) reader.getFilePointer()`, or `log.maxOffset()` when this is the last section, before `requestTermination()`. Alternatively, track clean end-of-section separately from the error flag and update position in both cases.

findings.rule: State read twice / ordering: derived state assumes a stable view (checklist 9, 19)
findings.problem: After the segment iterator is exhausted, position is set unconditionally to log.maxOffset() instead of the offset actually reached. For an in-progress (not completed) segment, the iterator can stop early on an unsynced or partially written trailing section. Position then jumps past bytes that were never read, and the marker handed to the caller or persisted CDC state skips them. On resume those mutations are never read. maxOffset is also read at a different time than the data, so it can differ from what was actually consumed.
findings.fix: Set position to the actual reader.getFilePointer() or the last fully consumed section end. Raise it to maxOffset only when log.completed() is true and the whole file was consumed.
findings.title: Do not jump position to maxOffset when the iterator ends before it

findings.problem: The new guard `if (statusTracker.shouldContinue())` skips updating position whenever readSection called requestTermination(). That is correct for the end-of-segment marker, which now sets maxOffset itself. The other benign termination, `end - reader.getFilePointer() < 4` at about line 436, sets no position. If a section ends with fewer than 4 trailing bytes (the 2.1-era case the code comment describes), the mutations of that section are emitted but position stays at the previous value. The listener emits the stale marker and the loop breaks, so later sections are never read. Result.isFullyRead() stays false and the next microbatch re-reads the same section. This is the same stall the ticket describes and produces duplicate mutations. Before the patch, position still advanced to reader.getFilePointer() on this path.
